reason: Reproduced by measurement, not by eye. Range client rects on .b-when give lines [260, 73] — '2026' alone — at owner-flight@390, owner-editing@390, desk@390, print@390, print@1280 and print@1440, exactly the six cases named; the printed keepsake orphans the year at every desk width. .b-ogDate on the share card gives [209, 32] at publish@390, also as claimed. .b-behindNote gives [332, 87] at phone@390, phone@768, and at owner-flight/owner-editing/desk on 1280 and 1440 (the 'every single width' phrasing is loose — at 390 in the non-phone states it breaks 251/168, which is fine — but the defect is real at every viewport). .b-pressBody ends [501, 469, 153] at 768 and above. grep confirms there is no text-wrap, no balance, no pretty and no non-breaking space anywhere in b.css, shell.css or fixture.js; computed textWrap is 'wrap' on every one of these blocks, so the breaks are unset, not chosen. Neither audit.mjs nor interaction-check.mjs asserts anything about line breaking, so this is not a restatement of a gate. It costs no colour and no weight. BUT the fix as written is wrong and would ship a worse defect than the one it cures — see sharpenedFix.
sharpenedFix: Do not emit 'Saturday 3 October 2026'. I tested that exact string: fully non-breaking, the line measures 340px inside a 278px header at 390 and a 280px sheet in print, so it overflows — document scrollWidth goes 390 -> 396 (the phone page scrolls sideways) and the print sheet's most ceremonial line runs past its own measure at 1280 and 1440. Trading an orphaned year for a clipped year on the keepsake is a net loss. Two corrections. (1) Bind only the month to the year: 'October 2026'. Measured, that yields [144, 189] on .b-when and [145, 96] on .b-ogDate at 390 — a clean 'Saturday 3 / October 2026'. (2) Do not put the NBSP in fixture.js's shared fmt.longYear: that same formatter feeds an editable <input value=...> at render-a.js:232 and render-c.js:195, and an invisible NBSP in a field the operator types into is a bug in waiting. Add a display-only sibling (fmt.longYearTight) and call it from .b-when, .b-ogDate and .b-dayDate only. Cleaner still: `text-wrap: balance` on .b-when and .b-ogDate alone produces the identical [144, 189] / [128, 112] result with no string mutation at all and applies in print layout too, so the CSS half of the fix makes the fixture half unnecessary for these two classes — take that route and drop the NBSP entirely. Keep balance on .b-emptyTitle (167/158/140 at 390) and .b-endedTitle; .b-dayNames never wraps at any width, so leave it. Finally, scope the proposed gate: 'no last line under 30% of the first' is both wrong-shaped and set on a knife edge — .b-pressBody already sits at 153/501 = 30.5% and would flip red on a font-metric change, .b-emptyBody@390 is 40/140 = 28% and has no fix but a copy edit, and .b-foot carries the 43-character share token with overflow-wrap:anywhere and would fail outright. Assert instead, over a named allowlist of prose and headline classes, that no last line is a single word shorter than six characters and that no last line is under 25% of the block's widest line.
